topic: Project: R.I.O. – Personal AI Runtime & Autonomous Agent System
content: R.I.O. (2025) is Bala Mugesh's Personal AI Runtime & Autonomous Agent System in Python. It converts natural-language and voice goals into structured execution plans using LLM task reasoning, DAG orchestration, tool routing, verification, and failure recovery. Stack: Groq LLMs, Whisper STT, FastAPI, WebSockets, PyTorch, CUDA. It supports persistent voice interaction and multi-step computer automation with permission boundaries between AI reasoning and OS execution, plus adaptive routing across remote LLMs and a local RTX 4050 GPU with resource-aware parallel execution and evidence-based verification. It is validated with 300+ automated and live acceptance tests, including LLM output-quality and hallucination checks.

content: PMT Analytics Dashboard (2026) at Appxcess Technologies replaced a spreadsheet-based reporting process with a Python analytics backend (Flask, FastAPI microservices) and a Next.js frontend. topic: Project: ConsensusIQ – Multi-Device AI Visual Inspection System
content: ConsensusIQ (2026) is a distributed multi-device AI visual inspection system built for Qualcomm's Snapdragon Multiverse Hackathon, splitting inference across edge and telemetry nodes. YOLOv11n was trained on 33,000+ synthetic images containing 62,000+ defects, with live results streamed to a FastAPI + React dashboard.

ResolveTrace (2026) mines Condition → Action → Outcome decision pathways from 28K+ reconstructed support conversations (SpotifyCares Twitter data), producing 1,545 pathways and a 3-state decision engine (auto-handle, escalate, unknown). Its hybrid matcher (TF-IDF retrieval + structured state compatibility) was benchmarked against a semantic RAG baseline on 212 gold test cases: pathway accuracy improved to 0.590 vs 0.524, and false auto-handling was reduced from 11.8% to 5.0%. It includes drift monitoring (rolling Jensen-Shannon divergence), LLM-judge + human-annotated reply-quality evaluation, FastAPI + Streamlit UI, and 19 unit tests.
